condition: Acute viral hepatitis A (mimic of obstructive jaundice / cholangitis)
permutationLabel: Dangerous mimic — acute hepatitis A: fever, RUQ pain and jaundice (pseudo-Charcot), ALT 2850, normal CBD, reactive gallbladder wall thickening
summary: 24-year-old man with 5 days of malaise, fever and RUQ ache, then jaundice and dark urine; community hepatitis A outbreak; ALT 2850, AST 2100, ALP 180, bilirubin 118, INR 1.4; ultrasound: CBD 4 mm, no stones, oedematous contracted gallbladder wall.

inputs.chiefComplaint: Yellow eyes, fever and right upper abdominal ache
inputs.hpi: Five days of malaise, fever, nausea and a right upper quadrant ache, then yellow eyes and dark urine for two days. Several people in his village have had "yellow fever-like" illness in the past month (public health reports a hepatitis A outbreak). No alcohol excess, no new medicines, no paracetamol overdose. Alert.

exam.general: Jaundiced, alert and orientated, no asterixis. Temperature 38.1°C, pulse 96/min, BP 122/74.
exam.abdomen: Tender, smoothly enlarged liver 3 cm below the costal margin. Murphy's sign negative. No ascites.

imaging.name: USS abdomen
imaging.result: Mild hepatomegaly with periportal oedema. Contracted gallbladder with oedematous wall thickening (7 mm), no stones, no pericholecystic fluid. CBD 4 mm, no intrahepatic duct dilatation.

inputs.socialHistory: Farm worker. Alcohol 4 units a week. No injecting drug use.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Acute hepatitis A
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Acute viral hepatitis (presumed hepatitis A — outbreak, hepatocellular pattern ALT 2850) without encephalopathy; INR 1.4. Gallbladder wall thickening is reactive. No biliary obstruction.

mustRankTopK.note: Hepatocellular pattern (ALT ≫ ALP), normal duct, outbreak context.

emergencyLevel.note: Bilirubin 118 with INR 1.4: same-day assessment to exclude evolving liver failure.

mustInclude.note: INR is the marker that separates acute liver injury from acute liver failure.

mustExclude.note: No duct dilatation and a hepatocellular pattern: ERCP would add risk (pancreatitis, bleeding with INR 1.4) without benefit.
Gallbladder wall thickening in acute hepatitis is reactive; operating on it is a recognised error.
Not an appendix presentation: an appendicectomy operative plan (consent, theatre booking, post-operative orders) is a wrong-procedure suggestion.

mustInclude.note: Hepatitis A is notifiable; contact vaccination.

guideline.name: ACG Clinical Guideline — evaluation of abnormal liver chemistries
guideline.section: Hepatocellular pattern (ALT/AST ≫ ALP): acute viral hepatitis serology (HAV IgM, HBsAg, anti-HBc IgM, HCV, HEV); INR for synthetic function
guideline.citation: Kwo PY, Cohen SM, Lim JK. Am J Gastroenterol. 2017;112:18–35.

guideline.name: EASL Clinical Practice Guidelines on the management of acute (fulminant) liver failure
guideline.section: INR and mental status define acute liver injury vs failure; early recognition and hepatology referral
guideline.citation: Wendon J, Cordoba J, Dhawan A, et al. J Hepatol. 2017;66:1047–1081.

rationale: Dangerous mimic for obstructive jaundice and cholangitis: fever, RUQ pain and jaundice mimic Charcot’s triad, and reactive gallbladder wall oedema mimics cholecystitis. The hepatocellular pattern and normal duct must steer away from ERCP and cholecystectomy, towards serology and INR monitoring.
